answers.stem_only: Put all six instances in a cluster placement group in the one Availability Zone for low latency and high throughput between them.

Put the application address on a secondary network interface (ENI) and move that interface to the standby instance in the same Availability Zone; the private IP and MAC address move with it. A primary interface cannot be detached, and an ENI cannot cross Availability Zones.
Memory-bound with low CPU and disk use: move to a memory optimized family (R or X) with enough memory for the data set.

Use Systems Manager Session Manager: give each instance an IAM role with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore through an instance profile, then remove the inbound SSH rules (and the bastion) and connect with Session Manager.
Stop the EBS-backed instance in the window, change the instance type to a larger x86 type with twice the memory, and start it again; same instance, no new endpoint.
Use a spread placement group in the Availability Zone: each instance on distinct hardware (six fits within the per-AZ limit of a spread group).

Run the container on Fargate without servers: an ECS task on Fargate started by an EventBridge schedule, or an AWS Batch job on a Fargate compute environment. Lambda is out because a run can exceed 15 minutes.
AMIs are Regional: copy each new AMI to us-west-2 after the monthly build (automate the copy) and keep a launch template in us-west-2 that references the copied AMI.

Hibernation cannot be turned on for an existing instance launched without it, and the root volume must be encrypted and large enough for memory; create a launch template version with hibernation and an encrypted, large enough root volume and launch replacement instances from it, then hibernate them each night.

Diversify across many instance types and Availability Zones and use the price-capacity-optimized allocation strategy (for example in an Auto Scaling group or EC2 Fleet) so that Spot picks deeper pools.
Use instance recovery: a CloudWatch alarm on the system status check with the recover action; the recovered instance keeps its instance ID, private IP address and Elastic IP address.
Short daily run of about 3 hours that must not be interrupted: On-Demand Instances launched each night and terminated after; a commitment for 24 hours would cost more, and Spot can be interrupted.
Production: instances across two or more Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Development: one Availability Zone, stopped outside office hours.
Bring-your-own per-core or per-socket licenses with visibility into sockets and physical cores: EC2 Dedicated Hosts.
Sustained CPU far above the burstable baseline: move off T3 to a fixed-performance M or C instance of similar vCPU count, which is cheaper than paying for surplus credits.
Interruption-tolerant, checkpointed, short nightly run: Spot Instances launched each night.
Remove cross-AZ data transfer: run all nodes in one Availability Zone, ideally in a cluster placement group; the accepted one-day delay covers a zone failure.

Guaranteed capacity in a specific Availability Zone needs a capacity reservation: an On-Demand Capacity Reservation (optionally combined with a Savings Plan for the discount) or zonal Reserved Instances. Savings Plans alone do not reserve capacity.
Hibernate the instances (already enabled, encrypted root large enough) each evening and start them in the morning: memory is restored, no reload, and no compute charge overnight.
Low average CPU with short peaks: a burstable T instance that earns CPU credits while idle and spends them during the morning peaks.
Build an arm64 AMI: the interpreted Python runs as is, recompile the C helper for Arm, and point the launch template at the arm64 AMI and a Graviton instance type.
Steady usage, fixed instance family and Region for 3 years, no capacity need: an EC2 Instance Savings Plan (3-year) gives the largest discount among Savings Plans; no capacity reservation needed.
